title: Pocketbridge claimflow intake — raw onramp ramble
content:
Quick dump after 01/11 sync with Pocketbridge (CPO + infra + security). Mostly notes to self and action items. Not polished.

Call context:
- Pocketbridge: mid-market P&C insurer, focusing on automated FNOL (first notice of loss) and triage.
- Pilot goal: deploy lightweight claim intake assistant to reduce initial adjuster triage time (~30% target).
- Constraints: PHI-like PII (SSNs, policy numbers), US-only infra, strict audit logs, encryption at rest + KMS integration.
- Team on call: Sam (CPO), Dr. Lee (Head of Data), Javier (infra), legal on standby.

High-level ask from customer:
- Low-latency conversational intake for web/mobile (p95 < 350ms for short utterances, target < 250ms if we can).
- Deterministic extractors for: claimant name, policy id, incident date, incident type, vehicle info, injuries.
- Redaction pipeline: customer requires redaction before any payload leaves their VPC (prefer on-client or at ingress).
- Audit trail: all model responses and extraction confidence must be logged with per-request correlation id for 365 days.
- Rollouts: start on Redwood Hosted via dedicated tenant, then move to Redwood Private (VPC) within 8–10 weeks if pilot metrics good.

Technical notes / gotchas called out during call:
- They operate in an air-gapped-ish AWS org with strict egress policies; will require Private deployment or a strict VPC-peered hosted route. Javier insisted on no plaintext policy numbers in logs.
- Redaction: they asked for client-side pseudonymization + server-side double-check. Need to confirm which fields to pseudonymize vs hash. Also asked whether we can run a regex-based scrub BEFORE tokenization (important for not leaking to model).
- Token accounting: they are cost sensitive. Their sample session shows long back-and-forth (avg ~200 tokens/session). Need batching options / prefix-caching for repeated follow-ups (FAQ-style).
- Model determinism: they want stable extraction outputs to avoid downstream reconciliation churn. Suggest we use a small extractor model fine-tuned/templated for high-precision fields and run the LLM only for conversational NLP.
- Latency: they plan to shard traffic across mobile/web with many short messages; runtime needs to prioritize single-turn latency over batch throughput. Consider dedicated low-batch queues or fast path on Dedicated.
- Attachments: they may upload 1–3 images (accident photos). Need to pipeline OCR -> redact -> summarize before sending to LLM. OCR latency risk.

Preliminary requirements (candidate):
- Data residency: US-only (us-west-2 + us-east-1).
- Security: KMS integration (customer-managed key preferred), audit logs exported to their SIEM (S3 + Kinesis).
- API: REST + websocket support for streaming partial responses.
- SLA targets: p95 latency < 350ms for textual prompts (<= 128 tokens), 99.5% availability during business hours, token usage reports weekly.
- Rollout phasing: PoC (hosted sandbox) -> pilot (dedicated reserved capacity) -> private VPC (if legal signs).

Architecture notes — suggested approach:
1) Frontend: client-side regex redaction for obvious fields (SSN, policy id formats). Replace with placeholders (PB_POLICY_XXXX) and keep mapping in ephemeral store.
2) Ingress validation service (customer infra): OCR for attachments, deterministic extractors (rules + small model), redact/normalize, then forward to Redwood endpoint via VPC peering.
3) Redwood serving: small extractor model (opt) + chat model for clarifying Qs. Use prefix caching for repeated policy-context prompts to reduce token usage. Provide deterministic extractor responses to be the primary source of truth for structured fields; LLM output for free text summaries only.
4) Logging: store original (redacted) request + extractor outputs + LLM reply hash + correlation id. Expose export to S3 (encrypted).

Open questions (must confirm):
- Which exact fields MUST NEVER leave in plaintext? (Sam said policy numbers, SSNs, DOBs). Need canonical list.
- Do they want client-side redaction (recommended) or will they accept server-side redaction inside VPC?
- How many concurrent users expected during pilot? Sam guessed 60–120 active sessions/day; need peak concurrent to size Dedicated pool.
- Attachment OCR SLA: acceptable extra latency per attachment? If > 800ms, UX will degrade on mobile.
- Legal: retention policy (365 days vs 7 years for claims). If long retention, log storage cost estimate needed.

Risks / implications for Redwood:
- If they require client-side pseudonymization and strict no-PII egress, Hosted product will need a VPC-peering or Private option — impacts sales motion and timeline.
- Need to validate KMS/customer-managed-keys flow for key rotations and log exports.
- Deterministic extraction implies additional model management (versioning, eval sets). Might be extra work from research/applied-ml to ship a small extractor.

Immediate next steps (who/when):
- Asha: send follow-up email with list of canonical sensitive fields + ask for expected peak concurrent sessions (due 2025-01-14).
- Tom: spin up quick cost estimate for Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (include storage for 365d logs) and put numbers in the Confluence page (due 2025-01-16). Linked artifact: CONFLUENCE-CLM-PBX-7.
- Riley: prototype a strawman pipeline diagram (OCR -> redact -> extractor -> LLM) and mock latency numbers (due 2025-01-20).
- Infra (action TBD): confirm whether VPC peering will be acceptable or if full Private deploy is required; schedule call with Javier week of 01/20.
- Legal: request a copy of their data retention / compliance checklist (Asha to CC legal).

Notes to self / prompts I want to run with Eng & Research:
- Evaluate lightweight extractor options: pattern-based + distilled classifier for policy id extraction — emphasis on precision (>= 98%) even at expense of recall.
- Consider running extractor as a local microservice in the customer's VPC for zero-egress of structured PII (only hashes exported).
- Build a quick eval harness with sample transcripts from Pocketbridge (ask for sanitized examples).

Random messy observations from call:
- Sam: "we'd rather have slightly slower but auditable and reproducible outputs than magical hallucinations" — emphasize deterministic extractor & confidence scores.
- Javier repeatedly: "No plaintext policy numbers in your logs" — underline again.
- They use an internal ticket ID format starting with PB-YYYY-#### — can exploit to anchor extractor heuristics.

Draft email outline to send after call (Asha):
- Quick thanks + recap of constraints (VPC, KMS, redaction, retention)
- Ask for sanitized sample transcripts + sample attachments (images)
- Request peak concurrency & expected daily sessions
- Propose next technical sync with infra + security (week of Jan 20)

- [ ] Prototype extractor latency/precision (owner: Riley)
- [ ] Schedule infra deep-dive (owner: Asha/Tom)

-- end of raw notes --
